summary: Console filtered-population spike: usage counts drop after tracehook token rotation
description:
Issue summary:
After a scheduled tracehook token rotation for Sketchly Media on 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC, their console dashboard's filtered population counts for route-scoped usage dropped to near-zero for a subset of routes. The unfiltered totals (org-level) remain unchanged. This caused downstream alerting (SLO spike alerts) and customer-reported incorrect per-route billing previews.

Impact:
- Several per-route usage sparklines and "route population" panels show 0-2 events for a 3-hour window that previously had thousands/hour.
- SLO/alert thresholds triggered for a short window due to apparent drop.
- Customer-facing billing preview shows missing route attribution which affects internal chargeback.

Environment:
- Customer: Sketchly Media (enterprise), org-id sk-3321
- Deployment: prod, us-east region
- Components touched: console route attribution, tracehook token rotation job, usage-ingest microservice

Steps to reproduce (as performed by Support):
1) Impersonated customer route (org-scoped API key) and viewed Dashboard > Usage > Route Population (last 6h) for route rt-sketchly-feed.
2) Noted gap beginning ~2026-03-10 02:05 UTC.
3) Queried raw events via ad-hoc export covering the same window; unfiltered events exist and show normal counts.
4) Replayed the route-scoped query with tracehook header present vs absent; only requests with the older tracehook token were attributed to the route panels.

Observed behavior:
- Console panels that filter by tracehook-anchored route attribute drop events if the incoming request's tracehook token does not match the active token cached by the console lookup service. The ingest pipeline still records events, but the join used for route attribution fails when token rotation occurs mid-window.

Expected behavior:
- Rotation should be transparent: historical events within the time window should be attributed by route using a short grace window for token acceptance or by correlating alternate route identifiers. Dashboard filters should not show a false zero population.

Investigation notes:
- Tracehook rotation job ran at 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC (job id rotate-20260310-02).
- Tracehook-proxy pod rotated tokens and pushed new token to key-cache while console's route-lookup cache still referenced the prior token until cache TTL expiry (TTL was 5m).
- Usage-ingest stores raw events with header tracehook.token value. When console applies filter-by-route it performs a lookup against current token->route mapping. Because the rotation replaced the mapping atomically, events with the old token in the window lost their route mapping until the migration job backfilled legacy tokens into the lookup map.
- SRE logs: tracehook-proxy logs show a spike of 429s to the route-lookup endpoint at 02:01 UTC, followed by repeated cache misses.
- Query sample: raw event ids [evt-98321, evt-98322, evt-98345] (timestamps 02:03-02:08 UTC) present in raw export but missing from route panel.

Relevant links:
- Slack thread: #support Sk-3321 (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C06SUPPORT/p1678550400000)
- Console panel: https://console.redwood.com/org/sk-3321/dashboards/usage/rt-sketchly-feed
- Runbook: Tracehook Rotation Runbook (Confluence link above)

Workaround implemented:
- Support toggled the console route-lookup service to accept both legacy and current tracehook tokens for the window 02:00-02:10 UTC which restored route counts in the panel.
- We advised customer to temporarily disable automated alerting on the affected SLOs until attribution correction finished.

Next steps (in progress):
1) Engineering to update tracehook rotation job to write a short-lived token alias mapping for the previous token covering 10 minutes after rotation (ENG-PR planned).
2) Add a console-side fallback to check raw event metadata fields (route header fallback) before classifying as "unattributed".
3) Short-term: reduce route-lookup cache TTL to 30s and add a targeted retry when cache miss spikes are detected.
4) Postmortem and customer follow-up with timeline and billing reconciliation.

Resolution notes:
- Partial workaround applied; full mitigation pending ENG-PR and patch deployment. Will update ticket when patch is released.
comments: Support (Maya Ortiz) - 2026-03-10: Initial triage complete. Confirmed raw events are present; issue appears to be attribution in console only. Customer is impacted (billing/alerts). Escalating to SRE.

SRE (Liam Chen) - 2026-03-11: Identified token rotation event and cache TTL mismatch. Implemented temporary acceptance of legacy token on route-lookup and validated route counts restored. Preparing PR to mitigate.
Customer (Raj Patel, Sketchly) - 2026-03-11: Thanks — counts look normal again. We need a timeline for a permanent fix; this caused duplicate alert noise for our ops team.

Engineering (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-12: Reviewing runbook and will open PR to add alias mapping and improve rotation handshake. Will include unit tests and canary rollout plan. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tracehook-proxy/pull/742
